paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: you don't get to God's wisdom by being clever, you get there by being given it. Paul came to Corinth in "weakness and fear, and with much trembling" (1 Corinthians 2:3), with no fancy speech, and he did it so their faith would rest "not on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power" (1 Corinthians 2:5). If the message had needed a smooth talker, the credit would've gone to the talker. I've been a stamper in a junk drawer, so trust me, I'm NOT the talent in this operation!

No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined what God has prepared for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9), so how do we know any of it? "God has revealed it to us by the Spirit" (1 Corinthians 2:10). Paul says nobody knows a man's thoughts except his own spirit, and "no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God" (1 Corinthians 2:11). That means understanding God isn't a prize for the smartest person in the room, it's a gift from the One who already knows Him.

And that matters for you, baker. When the message of the cross feels like foolishness to somebody, Paul says that's because it is "spiritually discerned" (1 Corinthians 2:14), so you don't have to win the argument or sound impressive. You can stay with Scripture and ask the Spirit to teach you, because Paul says "we have the mind of Christ" (1 Corinthians 2:16). Keep your eyes on Jesus Christ and Him crucified (1 Corinthians 2:2), and let God do the heavy lifting. Stay close, because Paul's letter to this church isn't done yet.
